title: Behenian plant-part qualifiers may be compositional operators rather than new whole names
summary: The roster explicitly contrasts an unqualified Mandrake with the root of Mandrake and Perwinkle with flowers of Perwinckle; a target can encode the same base item with a part modifier without requiring one identical whole form.
mechanism: A reusable base item is combined with a source-defined plant-part operator. The operator changes the material role while the base recurrence remains a cross-row relation.
target_endpoint: GDT960's already admitted fifteen-group object; target forms and keys were not read in this task.

two_readings.name: base-plus-part operator
two_readings.claim: Rows 4 and 10 use Mandrake as a base material while row 15 adds the narrower root qualifier; row 8's flowers of Perwinckle likewise differs from row 10's Perwinkle.
consequences: A target candidate may share an internal component across the related positions while its complete form changes when the part operator is present.
The qualified positions must occupy a distinct material-part role; collapsing root/flowers into the unqualified item erases a source-attested relation.

two_readings.name: opaque independent row labels
two_readings.claim: Each complete row entry is an independent label; repeated plant strings are ordinary reuse and qualifiers are descriptive prose with no compositional target operator.
consequences: No shared internal component is required between qualified and unqualified entries.
The same target whole may be reused or omitted without a predictable part-conditioned change.

smallest_distinguishing_observation: On the already admitted GDT960 fifteen-group endpoint, predeclare a comparison of repeated internal components and their local role classes: a base recurrence with a second component only at source-qualified positions supports the operator model; no such component-conditioned split leaves the opaque-label rival viable. Do not assign any component an English plant name.
strongest_failure: No target form-to-part binding is independently available yet, and the 1651 English witness may preserve editorial descriptive wording rather than a code-like part grammar. A component overlap could also be ordinary reusable morphology.
falsifier: Reject if every candidate representation either forces identical complete forms for qualified and unqualified entries or requires posthoc splitting/merging with no fixed source-part rule.
assumption_costs: GDT960's fifteen-group endpoint can be fixed before semantic assignment.
The target has a reusable component layer capable of representing a base-plus-qualifier relation.
The source's explicit plant-part wording is relevant to the target's content family.
review_note: This is a source-grounded relation hypothesis, not a Mandrake/Perwinkle gloss and not an endorsement of GDT960's untested plant-incidence model.
